report.warm_baseline: the exact first-complete-cycle scalar fixture record

nonclaims: does not consume or unblock an M5 gate
does not establish general cross-thread, post-exit, upstream-pthread, or large-object acceptance
does not establish a selected or default crabc-libc native-mimalloc allocator backend

caller_contract: The fixture is one fresh Linux/AArch64 process and calls init once with its original thread's nonzero AT_PAGESZ value.
Every allocation, reallocation, and free is serialized on that original thread.

After the original thread frees every adapter allocation, one fresh pthread may make one pointer-free narrow worker round trip or one pointer-private persistent mixed-local worker round trip; either creates and finishes one later-main page engine before its normal worker teardown.

The persistent worker keeps one engine through multiple simultaneously live small, medium, large, singleton, and multi-page singleton allocations, checks their contents, locally reuses freed small and medium blocks, and frees every block before engine finish; no pointer crosses the worker boundary.

After the original thread frees every adapter allocation, one fresh pthread may become remote-free owner A. The adapter starts and joins two private publisher pthreads B/C; only opaque logical publication capabilities reach them, A false-collects and reuses both remote blocks while still live, and then A frees every block before normal teardown.

After every scheduled worker joins, the original thread may request one test-only scalar lifecycle audit. It reports process/page-owner readiness and aggregate PageMap, arena registry, live-TLD, metadata-capability, shared-Theap, regular-abandoned, and OS-abandoned-list state only; it cannot identify or operate on a pointer, page, route, allocator, or release capability. The first complete schedule cycle warms immutable capacity; every later cycle and the final ticket-zero allocation/free must reproduce that quiescent snapshot.
Only current pointers returned by this adapter may reach its realloc or free entry points.
No shutdown is exposed: the permanent source-shaped ticket-zero page owner remains live until process exit.
The adapter exports no malloc, free, or mi_* ELF symbol and never selects crabc-libc's production backend.
fixture_observations: init, malloc, realloc, zalloc, and free preserve the caller's errno on their successful paths
the first ordinary allocation activates one real ticket-zero page-owner allocation
after all exact allocations free, the owner releases only its Rust PageMap lifecycle lease
one fresh worker can borrow that dormant published pair for the retained narrow scoped page-engine round trip and finish its normal attachment

the default three, or one caller-selected bounded count of, fresh workers can each retain one engine through the pointer-private mixed local small/medium/large/singleton/multi-page workload, locally reuse freed small and medium blocks, free all blocks, and restore normal attachment teardown

the default three, or one caller-selected bounded count of, fresh remote-free owners A can each create and join B/C, publish two exact full-small-page blocks through the real remote head, false-collect and reuse both while A stays live, free all blocks, and restore normal attachment teardown

the fixture accepts no arguments for its default three worker cycles and default unsigned-64-bit schedule seed, or at most one each of `--worker-cycles N` for decimal N in 1..1024 and `--stress-seed SEED` for a base-0 unsigned-64-bit literal in either order; every cycle executes each of the two pointer-private worker routes exactly once in a deterministic seed-shuffled order. The first completed cycle is the scalar lifecycle-audit warmup; each later cycle and the final ticket-zero allocation/free must match that audit's quiescent baseline. `allocator --churn` selects 128 with seed `0xd1b54a32d192ed03` under a 30-second watchdog, while opt-in `allocator --soak` selects 1024 with seed `0x94d049bb133111eb` under a 180-second watchdog
ticket zero reactivates afterward through the same first arena

compile_requirements.compiler: musl-gcc from the pinned Linux/AArch64 container
